title: Seidor grew 30% to EUR 1.121bn in 2024 as a package-led SAP house, not a bespoke builder
content:
Seidor is recorded at EUR 1.121bn of 2024 revenue, up 30%, with about 10,000 staff, and is described as the largest Spanish SAP house alongside a Microsoft practice. The screen's verdict turns on none of those numbers: it is package-led rather than bespoke.

Growth at that rate normally reads as a positive signal, and here it works against the lead. Fast growth in a package practice means the machine that is working is configuration and rollout of a proprietary suite, so the firm has every reason to keep selling exactly that. Bespoke, client-owned systems are a different delivery motion with different margins, different staffing and a different sales conversation.

The deeper problem is that SAP already owns the system of record in those engagements. A layer whose value is holding the append-only, user-attributed record of decisions has to be positioned either beside or against the suite the practice exists to implement — a conversation a EUR 1.1bn SAP partner has no commercial reason to open.
